title: Oklahoma's 179-0 Win Over Kingfisher College in 1917
question: What is the most points Oklahoma has ever scored in a football game?
answer: Oklahoma's highest single-game total is 179 points, in a 179-0 win over Kingfisher College on September 29, 1917, at Boyd Field in Norman. Bennie Owen was the head coach.
summary: Oklahoma beat Kingfisher College 179-0 on Sept. 29, 1917, still the top mark on OU's single-game scoring list. Here's the story and the next-biggest blowouts.
body: The most points Oklahoma has ever put on the board came on September 29, 1917, when the Sooners beat Kingfisher College 179-0 at Boyd Field in Norman. It was the second game of Bennie Owen's 13th season as head coach, a week after a 99-0 opener against Central State Normal.

SoonerStats, which tracks OU's record book, ranks that game first on its list of the program's highest home-game scoring totals. The Oklahoma Daily headlined its report the next day with the line that the Sooner scoring machine swamped Kingfisher College 179 to 0.

It was not a one-off. Kingfisher was a regular on the schedule in those years, and the same list shows a 157-0 OU win over the Kingfishers in 1919, a 140-0 win over Southwestern Oklahoma State in 1916 and a 104-0 win over Kingfisher in 1911.

Context matters here. Football in the 1910s was a very different game, and the small colleges on the schedule were not close to OU's size. The 1917 Sooners went 6-4-1 and lost 44-0 at Illinois a few weeks after the Kingfisher game, so the huge scores were far from the whole story of the season.
Still, for a fan looking for the biggest number in the Sooner record book, 179 is the answer, and it still tops the home-game list that SoonerStats keeps.
